relevance_note: Single-patient LAD-I case report with an individual ITGB2 genotype: 'genetic analysis confirmed a homozygous ITGB2 mutation (c.844C>T; p.Arg282Trp), consistent with LAD Type I'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no tables. JSON built with a short Python script from hand-chosen values; every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. Two in-scope people: the index infant ('patient', rule 5) and an affected maternal cousin ('maternal cousin of patient', rule 2), who had delayed cord separation and recurrent infections in infancy but no stated diagnosis, sex or genetic testing; no variant row for the cousin. The healthy, untested parents get no rows (described only as healthy and non-consanguineous). Age at presentation is 42 days, but no age at onset, diagnosis or last evaluation is stated as such (follow-up was 4 months after starting prophylaxis), so those are not reported. Consanguinity recorded 'no' as stated ('non-consanguineous parents'), although the text adds that marriages within extended families are common in their community. Absence of pus is recorded as feature 'significant pus formation' excluded, and as checklist 'absence of pus formation' observed. Omphalitis checklist item recorded observed from 'signs of infection ... at the umbilical site' and the umbilical abscess; the paper never uses the word omphalitis for this patient. Failure to thrive excluded from 'appropriate growth' during the 4-month follow-up (D-27 normal finding). Complement and lymphocyte-subset results are whole investigations reported as normal; recorded as written ('abnormal complement system evaluation', 'abnormal T-cell and B-cell distributions') rather than more specific abnormalities. Functional evidence is the patient's own flow cytometry (CD18 on 1.8% of neutrophils), attached to her single homozygous variant. Variant type not stated by the authors. Minor inconsistency: cord separation is said to have 'occurred at 22 days of age' yet 'required sterile cutting in the hospital'; the culture/clindamycin sentence is repeated for skin lesions and the umbilical lesion.
